answer: Influence is priced as the reciprocal of cluster size, so a copper of identities sharing one stake divides rather than multiplies its weight. Each agent locks collateral at 20,000 POA, and the collateral at risk grows with headcount while cluster weight stays flat. Reaching quorum means crossing a juniper of independently attested links, so a fake cluster must be woven from costly real ties. Correlated faults slash the bonded group together, and an identity with no such kernel carries no weight and earns nothing.
